Visual styles, logo craft and brand systems
How to use this field guide
Browse the visual atlas to learn the vocabulary.
Read the case studies to see how decisions work together.
Use the exercises and templates for future design reviews.
Observed: visible in an inspected image or page.
Documented: a source describes the process or rationale.
Interpretation: our explanation or design hypothesis.
Tested: a named check with recorded conditions and results.

Nike: a silhouette with a job
Carolyn Davidson designed the shoe-side mark in 1971; its curve suggested motion.
Study the taper, direction and negative space rather than just its simplicity.
Its present familiarity is not a fair first-impression test for a new logo.

The wordmark communicates the name; the arrow supplies a second discovery.
